name: Point of Injury / Casualty Collection Point

placement_rationale.text: This entry represents the point-of-injury/forward-CCP end of the evacuation chain specifically, not the whole chain through to definitive care — its own text names the POI-to-CCP leg as the single riskiest segment precisely because it's the shallowest. A 2km siting lands inside doctrine.md §2's forward-CP depth (2-5km), the right neighborhood for the most operationally distinctive, most exposed end of a chain that runs much deeper behind it. Confirmed plausible at current depth, no change.

short_role: The first link in the evacuation chain — point-of-injury first aid and a forward collection point before movement toward stabilization care.
characteristics: Combat medic/buddy first aid at point of injury, then movement to a covered/concealed CCP
Ground-robot (UGV) and small-drone evacuation increasingly used for the most exposed final stretch to the CCP
From the CCP, casualties move rearward toward stabilization and then definitive care further back
employment_notes: The riskiest leg of the whole medical chain is the shortest one — moving a casualty from point of injury to the CCP within a zone under constant drone observation. That risk is exactly why ground-robot and drone casevac has grown: an unmanned platform can make that short exposed run without risking a second casualty.
contrast_vs_traditional: Traditional casevac assumed the most dangerous exposure was the vehicle move to the rear; here, the first few hundred meters under a persistent drone's view can be the most dangerous leg of the entire chain, which is why that specific segment is where ground robots and small drones have been adopted fastest rather than at the rear of the chain.
